title: Microexperiment rollout canvas and KPI ledger
content:
Purpose:
This is a working canvas for small-batch rollouts (aka microexperiments) used to validate performance, cost, and quality signals before a staged public ramp. The doc is intentionally lightweight: treat as a petri-dish for hypotheses + quick go/no-go signals.

TL;DR (one liner):
Run 3 small microexperiments across users/traffic slices with targeted KPI probes, confirm no more than 5% degradation on latency P95 and <2% negative quality drift on evaluation prompts, then proceed to phased ramp.

Context / Why microexperiments now:
- We want a faster safety net for model/infra changes that avoids full canaries (expensive and slow).
- Recent infra kernel change (INFRA-997) may alter P50/P95 characteristics on long-context requests.
- Product wants confidence on cost delta before enabling quantized model in Dedicated pools.

Stakeholders (quick):
- Product ops owner: Avery Chen (me)
- SRE/Observability: Liam O'Neill
- Serving runtime lead: Priya Singh
- Customer success (signal owners): Maya Gupta
- Decision authority for go/no-go: Product Ops + Eng SRE on call

Hypotheses to test (explicit):
1) Kernel change reduces per-token cost by 8-12% at 2048 seq for gpt-like models without >3% latency P95 regression.
2) KV-prefix cache remains effective for 60% of requests; cache miss footprint < 35% for target cohorts.
3) Quality (measured via curated prompt eval set) shows no systemic hallucination increase (>1.5%) post-change.

Target KPI panel (annotated ledger):
- Latency P50 (ms): target <= 75 (baseline 68)
- Latency P95 (ms): target <= 220 (baseline 200)
- HTTP error rate (5xx): target <= 0.1%
- Token cost delta (%): target <= +10% (prefer negative)
- Eval quality drift (top-1 accuracy on eval prompts): target <= -2% absolute
- QPS throughput per node: target >= baseline * 0.95
- KV cache hit rate: target >= 60%
- Fallback rate to lower-spec model: target <= 0.5%

Quick rollout phases (concise):
- Phase 0 (lab): internal infra + canary sim; synthetic load on staging cluster; duration 2 days. Owner: serving-runtime.
- Phase 1 (microexperiment A): 0.5% traffic for internal beta cohort (internal accounts + employees). Duration 24 hours. Owner: product-ops.
- Phase 2 (microexperiment B): 2% traffic to small external cohort (opt-in customers). Duration 48 hours. Owner: solutions-eng.
- Phase 3 (microexperiment C): 10% traffic ramp with aggressive observability (feature flags + rollout guardrails). Duration 72 hours. Owner: product-ops + SRE.
- Phase 4: decision window and phased ramp if signals green. Owner: leadership signoff.

Acceptance criteria (go to next phase):
- No KPI exceeds alert thresholds for the full duration (see monitoring thresholds below).
- No recurring user-impacting errors reported via CS (Maya to confirm).
- Automated eval set shows quality drift <= threshold.

Monitoring and alert thresholds (operational):
- Alert 1: Latency P95 > target by +20% sustained for 15m -> page SRE on-call, pause ramp.
- Alert 2: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10m -> auto-roll back flag and page SRE.
- Alert 3: Eval quality drift > 3% over baseline -> immediate rollback to previous model variant.
- Alert 4: Token cost increase > 25% -> ops review and potential rollback.
- Slack bridge: #prod-ops-launch (auto-post from observability every 5m)

Ownership matrix (short):
- Feature flag controls: product-ops (Avery)
- Metric definitions / dashboards: observability (Liam)
- Deployment tooling / infra changes: serving-runtime (Priya)
- Customer communication + opt-in: solutions-eng (Maya)
- Post-mortem: product-ops + SRE + solutions-eng

Dependencies / pre-reqs (tickets):
- INFRA-997 (kernel selection and perf tuning) -> must be merged to staging
- PROJ-4821 (feature flagging scaffolding) -> gating for phase toggles
- PR 63 (rollout-scripts) -> automation for rollback and canary toggles

Contingency playbook (short bullets):
- If Alert 1 or 2 during Phase 1: rollback flag to 0%, run postmortem, do not continue to Phase 2 until root cause validated.
- If quality drift observed only on a specific cohort: pause cohort traffic and open targeted investigation.
- If combination of cost+latency unacceptable: switch to non-quantized model variant and re-run microexperiment.

Notes / items to resolve (TO-DOs):
- Create a 50-item eval prompt set that covers hallucination, instruction-following, and safety edge cases (action: Priya + Maya).
- Confirm SLA wording for opt-in customers (legal review may be needed) -> assigned to Maya.
- Add synthetic replay harness for long-context p99 tests (engineering infra).
- Determine precise sampling window for quality probes (stratified by user-tier).

Post-launch checklist (if proceed to phased ramp):
- Daily cadence for first 7 days: ops standup summary in #prod-ops-launch, metric snapshot + anomalies.
- 72-hour post-Phase-3 review: decision to continue ramp or rollback.
- Tag all rollout commits with PROJ-4821 and archive dashboards for audits.
- Customer comms: send optional NPS pulse to opt-in cohort 7 days after exposure.

Quick lessons from previous microexperiment (notes):
- Small cohorts revealed a single prompt family causing token amplification; added a prefix filter prevented it.
- Observability lag (60s) masked short spikes; raised metric resolution to 10s for P95 in this run.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above.

Unresolved questions (short):
- Do we want automated rollback based on a single metric breach or require two correlated signals? (ops decision)
- How to weigh quality vs cost tradeoffs when cost saving is substantial but small quality drift occurs? (leadership policy)

Bottom line / immediate next steps (this doc as of 2025-02-18):
- Finish eval prompt set (Priya + Maya) by 2025-02-20.
- Merge INFRA-997 to staging and run Phase 0 synthetic load by 2025-02-21.
- Schedule Phase 1 microexperiment for 2025-02-24 window (Avery to coordinate flags).

Notes-to-self: keep this canvas alive and prune after final postmortem. This doc is an operational scaffold — use it to make quick, evidence-led go/no-go decisions.
